name: Video Hash Analysis
description: Computes perceptual hash sequences across frames and analyzes inter-frame hash distance distributions to detect the abnormal similarity clustering or instability patterns characteristic of AI-generated video.
algorithm: Video Hash Analysis — Statistical Pattern Analyzer
mechanism:
This method uses perceptual video hashing for forensic analysis:

1. **Perceptual Hash Computation**: A perceptual hash is computed per frame using established algorithms (pHash, dHash, wavelet hash). The hash captures the perceptual content summary — robust to minor modifications but sensitive to content changes.

2. **Temporal Hash Stability**: Frame-to-frame hash changes are tracked. Natural video shows smooth hash evolution. The method detects anomalous hash transitions — sudden hash changes without corresponding visual scene changes, or hash stability during what should be content changes (freeze-frame manipulation).

3. **Known Content Matching**: Frame hashes are optionally compared against databases of known deepfake content or original source material. Hash matching can identify specific deepfake videos or trace the source footage used in a face swap.

4. **Hash-Based Tampering Detection**: The ratio of frame-to-frame hash distance to visual change magnitude is analyzed. Manipulated frames may show hash distances disproportionate to the apparent visual change — indicating content modification below the perceptual threshold but detectable in the hash space.

5. **Multi-Resolution Hashing**: Hashes computed at multiple resolutions capture changes at different spatial scales. Face-swap deepfakes may produce normal hashes at coarse resolution (overall structure preserved) but anomalous hashes at fine resolution (detail-level generation artifacts), creating a resolution-dependent hash signature.
parameters:
Analysis type: statistical
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through video hash analysis analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
